task: find and book a tutor on a tutoring platform (Preply, Wyzant, italki, Varsity Tutors, Cambly, Outschool): search by subject or language, compare tutors on rates, reviews, and intro videos, pick one, and book or schedule a trial or lesson through to the booking confirmation; complete when the booked-lesson confirmation is on screen. Surface pinned: the CLIENT-side booking flow — tutor-side content (how to become a tutor, earnings) is off-task.

tree.label: Find and book a tutor
tree.note: 1 where the platform demands an account - at the door (jHfA, i3ok, XyTV, KIjj, cDu8, 7RrY), or only when the booking button is pressed (CWIs, cDu8's email gate, 7jo_'s verify wall); half the keepers arrive signed in. 2 before any lesson on the credit platforms (jHfA, i3ok), when the wall fires inside 7 (jMRd), or after a trial to prepay hours (zym-). then 3, then 4 as far as the user bothers - filters are opened far more often than applied. 5 picks one tutor and 5.5 reads it; a profile that fails loops back to 5.1. 6 configures the lesson, with 6.6 for the time. 7 commits in one of three ways set by the platform: pay from the wallet and wait for the tutor (italki), pay at a checkout (Preply, the plan credit in 7RrY), or send a message request and pay later (Wyzant). 8 reads whatever follows, which on italki and Wyzant is a pending request. two keepers skip 3 to 5 and start on a chosen tutor (htcf, jHfA's recommended shortcut).

children.label: Get into the platform
children.note: 1.1, then 1.2 or 1.3; 1.4 to 1.6 on a new account as the platform asks. 1.7 when the gate fires later, at the booking button - it can interrupt 7. 1.8 on the one keeper who lands on the wrong account type. 1.9 where offered, before the search, on the one keeper who opens settings.

questions.question: Do you already have an account here, or should I set up a new one?
questions.why: The screen requires authentication to view the 40,000+ tutor profiles, offering options to sign up via email or social accounts, or to sign in to an existing account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the choice of which personal account or authentication method is linked to their tutoring sessions.
questions.check: Does the page show a sign-in or sign-up prompt, and which options does it list (email, Google, Apple, Facebook)?
questions.say_example: This site needs an account before it shows any tutors. Do you already have one here? Say sign in, or say new account and I'll set one up.

questions.question: Does the sign-up page carry the free first hour promotion shown on the homepage?
questions.why: The current signup screen does not explicitly mention the free first hour, so navigating to the homepage might be necessary to trigger the promotional offer.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the financial benefit of a promotional discount if the agent defaults to the standard signup flow instead of hunting for the special offer.
questions.check: Does the sign-up page mention the free first hour promotion?
questions.say_example: Saw the free first hour promised on the homepage but not on the sign-up page. Checked at checkout whether it landed.

questions.question: Does the page promise a credit bonus for arriving through this link?
questions.why: The narrator explained that navigating through this specific link provides a $10 credit bonus when you purchase your first class.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the $10 promotional credit if the agent navigates directly to the platform instead of using the referral link.
questions.check: Does the page show a credit bonus for arriving through this link, and how much?
questions.say_example: Came in through a link that promised <10> credits. Checked at checkout whether it was applied.

questions.question: Is the site signed into your existing account, or is it creating a new one?
questions.why: The top navigation bar displays a 'Log in' link alongside options like 'Start free', which is necessary to access your saved profile and payment details for booking.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means the user loses the ability to ensure the agent signs into their specific existing account rather than accidentally creating a new one.
questions.check: Does the header show a signed-in account name, or still show 'Log in' / 'Start free' links, and does the name match the person's?
questions.say_example: I'm on a create-account page, but you said you already have an account here. Switching to sign in so your saved card and history are there.

questions.question: Is the Facebook account it wants to sign in with yours?
questions.why: The screen displays a prompt asking if you want to continue authenticating with a previously used Facebook account to access Preply.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to use their linked social media profile or a different method to authenticate their account.
questions.check: What name does the 'Continue as' prompt show?
questions.say_example: Facebook wants to continue as <name>. That's not you, so I've stopped. Which account should I use?

questions.question: Which sign-in option should I use? You'll type the password yourself.
questions.why: The sign-in form requires an email and password to authenticate your identity before you can proceed with the booking.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose control over which specific account is used to book the tutor and whether the session is kept signed in on the device.
questions.check: Does the page show email and password fields, and which other sign-in options are listed?
questions.say_example: The sign-in form is up. It offers <Google, Apple, or email>. Which one? The password is yours to type. Tell me when you're in.

questions.question: The site says the password didn't match. Do you want to retype it yourself?
questions.why: The screen displays an error message indicating invalid credentials, requiring you to identify the missing password and enter it to successfully authenticate.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to securely manage their own login credentials and troubleshoot authentication failures without exposing sensitive passwords to an agent.
questions.check: Does the page show an error such as 'credentials do not match' or 'incorrect password'?
questions.say_example: The site says the password didn't match. I won't guess at it. The field is yours.

questions.question: Is the email on the sign-up form spelled right?
questions.why: Double-checking the email field prevents typos that could lock you out of your new account or cause you to miss booking confirmations.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify that the account is registered to your exact, correctly spelled email address.
questions.check: What does the email field contain, and does the page show an error beside it?
questions.say_example: The email on the form reads <email>, one letter off from yours. Fixing it before I submit, or the confirmation goes nowhere.

questions.question: What does the sign-up form say you agree to by submitting it?
questions.why: The sign-up screen requires your email, name, password, and ZIP code, and clicking the sign-up button automatically binds you to Wyzant's terms of use and privacy policy.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to review the platform's terms of use and privacy policy before your personal information is submitted and the account is created.
questions.check: What text sits beside the sign-up button about terms of use and privacy?
questions.say_example: Sign-up asked for name, email, password, ZIP. Submitting agreed to <site>'s terms and privacy policy.

questions.question: Is the sign-up set to a parent account, since the lessons are for a child?
questions.why: Platforms like Outschool or Varsity Tutors require strict COPPA compliance, meaning lessons for children must be booked through a verified parent account with specific consent, not a standard adult learner profile.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user risks having the account banned or the lesson immediately cancelled by the tutor for violating child safety policies if the agent uses a standard profile.
questions.check: Does the sign-up form show a student age or account type choice, and which option is selected?
questions.say_example: This form has you down as an adult learner. The lessons are for <child>, so I'm switching to the parent account option. It will ask a parent to consent, and that part is yours.

questions.question: What name should show on your public profile?
questions.why: The name entered during registration is often displayed to tutors and potentially on public reviews, requiring a choice between using your real identity or a pseudonym for privacy.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over their privacy if the agent automatically uses their full legal name on a platform where they might prefer anonymity.
questions.check: Does the form say where the display name appears?
questions.say_example: Set the display name to <name>. The site shows it to tutors and on public reviews.

questions.question: The new account needs a password. Will you set it yourself?
questions.why: The screen requires a password of 6 or more characters where capitalization matters to proceed with the booking.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose your own secure and memorable password for your new tutoring account.
questions.check: Which fields does the sign-up form require, what password rule does it state, and what does it say you agree to by submitting?
questions.say_example: New account. It needs a name, which shows on your public profile, an email, and a password of <6> or more characters. I'll put <name> and <email>. The password is yours to type. Tell me when it's in and I'll continue.

questions.question: Is the personal-info form marked optional, so it can be skipped?
questions.why: The screen shows an email and personal info form that can be skipped by scrolling down.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the choice to withhold optional personal details to protect their privacy during checkout.
questions.check: Does the form label these fields optional or required, and is there a skip or continue button that works without them?
questions.say_example: Skipped the optional personal-info form.

questions.question: A reCAPTCHA is blocking the sign-up. Will you solve it yourself?
questions.why: The screen displays a reCAPTCHA grid requiring you to identify specific objects to prove you are human and proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to personally solve the visual security puzzle required to bypass the platform's bot protection.
questions.check: Does the page show a reCAPTCHA or 'prove you're human' challenge?
questions.say_example: There's a picture puzzle to prove you're human. That one's yours. Tell me when it's done.

questions.question: Do you want other learners to be able to contact you for language exchange?
questions.why: The onboarding modal requires you to specify if you are looking for a paid tutor and whether you want to receive language exchange requests.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to control your privacy and decide whether your profile is open to unsolicited language exchange requests.
questions.check: Does the onboarding modal ask whether to receive language exchange requests, and which option is selected?
questions.say_example: Said no to language exchange requests from other users.

questions.question: The form asks for your program of study and semester. What should I put?
questions.why: The onboarding form requires specific information like your program of study and semester to unlock the main booking calendar.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to accurately represent your specific academic background and preferred name on your tutoring profile.
questions.check: Which required fields on the form are empty, and what are their labels?
questions.say_example: The form won't go on without your program and semester. I don't have those. What should I put?

questions.question: What should I pick for how you heard about them?
questions.why: The checkout form includes a dropdown menu asking how you heard about the platform before allowing you to complete the booking.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to accurately report their actual referral source or give credit to the specific person who referred them.
questions.check: Does the form show a 'how did you hear about us' dropdown, and is it required?
questions.say_example: Picked Other for how you heard about them.

questions.question: Does the dashboard still say your email is unconfirmed after you clicked the link?
questions.why: Although you clicked the verification link, the dashboard still displays a red warning banner claiming your email is unconfirmed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might blindly assume the verification succeeded and fail to resolve the system error that could block the lesson booking.
questions.check: Does the dashboard still show a banner saying the email is unconfirmed?
questions.say_example: You clicked the link, but the site still says your email isn't confirmed. Messages from the tutor may not reach you until it clears. Resend the link, or wait a minute and reload?

questions.question: The site sent a confirmation link to your inbox. Will you click it yourself?
questions.why: The Wyzant email contains an orange confirmation button that must be clicked to verify your account and ensure you can receive correspondence from your tutor.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step requires granting the agent access to your personal email inbox, which exposes your private messages.
questions.check: Does the page say a verification link was sent, and to which address?
questions.say_example: The site sent a link to <email> and won't go on until it's clicked. That's in your inbox. Tell me when you've pressed it.

questions.question: After the email check, does the site go back to the tutor you were on, or to the dashboard?
questions.why: Although the screen prompts you with a 'GO TO DASHBOARD' button, using the OS task switcher allows you to bypass the generic dashboard and directly resume your previous search.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the seamless continuation of their specific search if the agent blindly clicks the dashboard button and loses the previous page's context.
questions.check: After verification, does the page show the dashboard or the tutor and search you were on?
questions.say_example: Went back to <tutor>'s page after the email check sent me to the dashboard.

questions.question: This is a tutor account, so it can't book. Do you want a student account made?
questions.why: The platform explicitly prevents booking from a tutor account and requires you to acknowledge the error before you can switch account types.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the awareness that your current account type is invalid for booking and the chance to decide how to set up a student profile.
questions.check: Does the popup say the account is a tutor account and that a student account is needed to book?
questions.say_example: This is a tutor account, so it can't book lessons. I can make a student account with <email>, or stop here. Which?

questions.question: Which email address should receive the lesson confirmation?
questions.why: The screen requires an email address to send the lesson booking confirmation and continue the process.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to choose which email address receives the booking confirmation or to abort the process.
questions.check: What email address is shown in the confirmation-email field?
questions.say_example: Set the confirmation email to <email>.

questions.question: Is the page on the student side of the site rather than the tutor side?
questions.why: The profile dropdown shows tutor-specific options like 'Insights' and 'Classroom', meaning you must switch to a student account to access the client-side booking flow.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If the agent fails to recognize it is logged in as a tutor, it will get stuck in the wrong dashboard and be unable to search for or book a lesson.
questions.check: Does the header, profile menu or page body show tutor-side items such as Insights, Classroom, or a tutor application?
questions.say_example: I've landed on the tutor side of the site. Nothing here books a lesson. Going back to the student side.

questions.question: The Google sign-in has stalled. Should I try email sign-in instead?
questions.why: The user attempts to log in with Google, switches tabs, and then abandons that route to click 'Get started' on the homepage instead, indicating a failure or change of mind with the authentication method.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might get stuck in a broken OAuth flow, failing to pivot to a standard email sign-up or alternative entry point to continue the task.
questions.check: Is the Google sign-in window still blank or loading after the click?
questions.say_example: The Google sign-in isn't going anywhere. Trying email sign-in instead.

questions.question: Which language do you want the app interface to display in?
questions.why: The profile settings screen includes an 'App language' option to customize the interface text.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might proceed in a default language that you cannot easily read if you need to review the booking later.
questions.check: What does the 'App language' setting show?
questions.say_example: Left the interface language at <English>.

children.label: Fund the account
children.note: 2.1 then 2.2, with 2.3 read against it; then 2.4 and 2.5. on italki this whole goal runs before a lesson is chosen (jHfA, i3ok) or fires as a wall inside 7 (jMRd). on Preply 2.6 picks the tutor first and the hours are prepaid for them (zym-). on Wyzant 2.7 is deferred until after the tutor replies (XyTV).

questions.question: What credit balance does the account page show?
questions.why: Checking the 'My Account' tab reveals your available funds, which dictates the price range you can afford when browsing search results.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose direct visibility into your current account balance and how it aligns with the rates of the tutors being considered.
questions.check: What balance does the account page show?
questions.say_example: Read the balance. <100> credits, about <10> dollars.

questions.question: How much do you want to buy up front, in credits or hours?
questions.why: The checkout screen defaults to a larger credit bundle and notes that buying more reduces transaction fees, requiring a choice between upfront investment and exact lesson cost.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to balance the potential savings of lower transaction fees against the financial commitment of holding excess credits on the platform.
questions.check: Which credit or hour amounts does the page offer, at what price each, and which one is preselected?
questions.say_example: You need to load money before booking. One lesson is <9>. The page has <20> hours preselected for <95>, which is <5> cheaper per lesson. Buy just the one, or the bundle?

questions.question: Does the selected payment method on screen match the one you stated you would use?
questions.why: The audio indicates a choice to use Skrill, but the screen shows the payment being processed with the Credit / Debit Card option still selected.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over their financial accounts if the agent charges a default card instead of the specifically requested payment method.
questions.check: Which payment method is shown as selected at checkout?
questions.say_example: You said <PayPal>, but the page still has <card> selected. Switching before I go on.

questions.question: Does the amount on the payment page match the site's checkout total?
questions.why: Verifying the total of $10.67 USD for 100 italki Credits ensures you are not being overcharged before logging into your payment account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the opportunity to catch hidden fees or discrepancies in the final billing amount before authorizing the payment.
questions.check: What total does the PayPal or card page show, and what total did the site's checkout show?
questions.say_example: PayPal is asking for <12.40>. The site's checkout said <10.67>. Those don't match, so I've stopped.

questions.question: Did the bonus credits promised on the front page show up after the purchase?
questions.why: The landing page explicitly promised a $10 credit voucher after the first purchase, but the final confirmation screen does not show it being awarded.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses out on a promised financial benefit because the agent failed to ensure the promotional credit was actually delivered.
questions.check: Does the confirmation or Transactions page list the promised <10> credit bonus?
questions.say_example: The front page promised <10> credits with your first purchase. The account shows the <100> you bought and nothing extra.

questions.question: Does the confirmation page show the credit purchase went through?
questions.why: The confirmation screen displays a green checkmark and an order number to verify that your funds were successfully converted into platform credits.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you miss seeing the exact order number and direct confirmation that your payment was successfully processed.
questions.check: Does the page show a success message or checkmark, the amount, and an order number?
questions.say_example: Paid. <100> credits for <10.67>, order <number>. Now the lesson.

questions.question: Does the account shown after payment match the one you used to initiate the booking?
questions.why: The screen suddenly displays a different profile with a pre-existing balance, a real photo, and scheduled lessons after the payment cut.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that their payment and booking were actually applied to their own account.
questions.check: What name, photo and balance does the profile show after payment, versus before?
questions.say_example: After paying, the page shows a different person: <name>, with lessons already booked. That's not your account. I've stopped.

questions.question: Is the total for the credits right before you pay?
questions.why: The checkout page displays a total of $190.30 including fees and a pre-checked auto-refill box that will automatically charge your saved card for future lessons.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over verifying the final transaction total and deciding whether to authorize automatic recurring payments.
questions.check: What total, fee line and payment method does the checkout show?
questions.say_example: Ready to pay. <190.30> for <20> hours, including a <0.72> card fee, on your <card ending 4821>. Press to pay, or say change.

questions.question: Is the tutor selected in the buy-hours modal the one you chose?
questions.why: The modal presents multiple tutors with different available actions, allowing you to either buy hours for a previous tutor or book a trial with a new one.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to continue investing time with a familiar tutor or try out someone new.
questions.check: Which tutor name is selected in the buy-hours modal, and which action (buy hours or book trial)?
questions.say_example: The buy box has <Kate> selected, from your old lessons. You picked <Marco>. Switching.

children.label: Set the search
children.note: 3.1 first, everywhere. 3.2 chooses the route: the questionnaire runs 3.3 to 3.8 one screen at a time with Skip on each, the manual route goes straight to 4. 3.9 is Wyzant's other door and 3.10 is italki's free alternative - both opened, neither taken further.

questions.question: Is the search set to your exact course code rather than the broad subject, so the tutors match your syllabus?
questions.why: Selecting the exact course code from the autocomplete dropdown ensures you find tutors who specialize in your specific class rather than a broad subject.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might search for a broad subject instead of your specific course code, potentially matching you with a tutor unfamiliar with your exact syllabus.
questions.check: What does the subject field show as selected: the course code or the broad subject name?
questions.say_example: The search picked the broad subject <Calculus>. You gave the course code <MATH 21>. Using the code, so the tutors match your class.

questions.question: Which specific subject or language do you want to search for?
questions.why: The platform presents a massive list of both academic subjects and languages, so picking the exact topic is necessary to filter the available tutors.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means missing out on browsing the extensive catalog of topics to find the exact skill or language you want to learn.
questions.check: Which subject or language does the search show as selected?
questions.say_example: The search is set to <Spanish>. You asked for <Portuguese>. Fixing it.

questions.question: Which language do you want to learn in this lesson?
questions.why: The tutor teaches multiple languages, so you must explicitly select which one you want to focus on for this booking.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure the lesson is taught in your target language, potentially wasting money on the wrong subject.
questions.check: Which language is selected in the booking's language dropdown?
questions.say_example: <Tutor> teaches more than one language. The booking has <Italian> picked. You want <Spanish>. Changing it.

questions.question: Should you take the matching questionnaire, or browse the full tutor list?
questions.why: The screen offers a choice between clicking 'Find your tutor' to answer a few quick questions for a personalized match or showing all 3,999 available French tutors.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally answer the questionnaire to ensure the platform's algorithm accurately captures your specific learning goals and preferences.
questions.check: Does the page offer a 'find your tutor' questionnaire and a link to browse all tutors?
questions.say_example: Skipped the matching quiz. Browsed all <3,999> tutors with your filters.

questions.question: What do you want out of the lessons?
questions.why: The platform asks for your learning goal, such as career advancement or exam prep, to tailor the tutor recommendations to your specific needs.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If the agent selects the learning goal for you, you might receive tutor recommendations that do not align with your actual reasons for studying.
questions.check: Which goal options does the page list, and is there a skip?
questions.say_example: Set the goal to <exam prep>, from your ask.

questions.question: How soon do you want to reach your goal?
questions.why: The platform asks for a target timeframe to tailor recommendations, offering options from a few weeks to indefinitely, or the choice to skip.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might skip the question or guess a timeframe, potentially leading to mismatched tutor recommendations or lesson pacing.
questions.check: Which timeframe options does the page list, and is there a skip?
questions.say_example: Set the timeframe to <three months>.

questions.question: What's your current level in the language?
questions.why: The platform asks for your French level, offering options from 'just starting' to 'fluent' or a skip button, to help filter and recommend appropriate tutors.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means the agent might guess your proficiency level incorrectly or skip the personalization entirely, leading to tutor recommendations that do not match your actual skill level.
questions.check: Which level options does the page list, and which is selected?
questions.say_example: Set the level to <beginner>, as you told me.

questions.question: What education level are you booking this tutoring for?
questions.why: The platform requires specifying if the student is an Adult, College, High School, Middle School, or Elementary level to filter for appropriate tutors.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting the agent guess the student's level could result in being matched with a tutor who specializes in the wrong age group or curriculum.
questions.check: Which education level options does the page list, and which is selected?
questions.say_example: Set the education level to <high school>.

questions.question: Which topic or exam do you want the lessons to focus on?
questions.why: The screen provides specific exam and topic options like DELF, TEF, and DALF that tailor the tutor recommendations to your exact needs.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means the agent might select the wrong certification or skip personalization entirely, resulting in tutors who cannot help you pass your specific exam.
questions.check: Which topic or exam options does the page list, and which is selected?
questions.say_example: Set the topic to <DELF>, since that's the exam you named.

questions.question: What kind of lessons are you looking for, like conversation or business?
questions.why: The platform prompts you to select a lesson focus, such as Conversational English or Business English, to filter for tutors who specialize in your goals.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to specify your exact learning objectives, which could result in the agent finding a tutor whose expertise doesn't match your needs.
questions.check: Which lesson focus options does the page list, and which is selected?
questions.say_example: Set the lesson type to <conversational>.

questions.question: Does the option selected on this step match what you asked for, or is it the site's default?
questions.why: The platform pre-selects a default topic like 'Conversational English' on the questionnaire, meaning clicking continue without changing it will skew your tutor recommendations.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the personalization of their search results if the agent blindly accepts the default topic instead of inputting their actual learning goals.
questions.check: Which option on this questionnaire step is shown as selected, and does it match the instruction?
questions.say_example: This step came preset to <Conversational English>. You asked for <IELTS prep>. Changing it before I continue.

questions.question: Do you prefer to meet with your tutor online or in person?
questions.why: The platform requires you to choose between online, in-person, or undecided formats to properly filter your tutor search results.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might select a meeting format that does not fit your learning style or physical location.
questions.check: Which format option is selected: online, in person, or undecided?
questions.say_example: Set the format to online, from your ask.

questions.question: Do you want to filter for tutors available within 72 hours?
questions.why: The search results page includes a 'Within 72 hours' checkbox to narrow down the list to teachers with immediate availability.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to prioritize immediate availability over a wider selection of tutors.
questions.check: Is the 'within 72 hours' box checked?
questions.say_example: Turned on within 72 hours, since you want to start this week.

questions.question: How soon do you need to start tutoring?
questions.why: The platform requires you to select a timeframe, ranging from today to sometime this month, to help match you with tutors who have appropriate availability.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might select a timeline that is either too urgent or too delayed for your actual learning goals.
questions.check: Which start-timeframe option is selected?
questions.say_example: Set the start to <this week>.

questions.question: Is the time zone the site picked the one you're actually in?
questions.why: If a user is traveling, using a VPN, or if a browser agent is running on a cloud server, the platform might auto-detect the wrong timezone for the calendar.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user misses the lesson and forfeits the fee entirely because the agent scheduled it based on a server's timezone rather than the user's actual local time.
questions.check: What time zone and country does the page show as current, in the modal or the calendar header?
questions.say_example: The site thinks you're in <Frankfurt>. You're on <Pacific time>, so every lesson time here would be <9> hours off. Setting it to <Pacific>.

questions.question: Do you want to manually search for a tutor or submit a request?
questions.why: Submitting a request can be a faster way to find a match for specific subjects compared to browsing individual profiles.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to decide whether you want to handpick a specific tutor yourself or let the platform match one to your needs.
questions.check: Does the page offer 'submit a request' alongside search?
questions.say_example: Searched tutors directly rather than posting a request, since you wanted a lesson booked.

questions.question: Do you want to look for a free language exchange partner instead of a paid tutor?
questions.why: The 'Community' dropdown includes a 'Find Language Partners' option, offering an alternative to standard paid lessons.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to decide if you prefer engaging in a free language exchange over booking a paid tutoring session.
questions.check: Does the menu offer a language-partner option?
questions.say_example: Skipped the free language-partner option. You asked for a tutor.

children.label: Narrow the list
children.note: 4.1 opens the surface. any of 4.2 to 4.8, in any order, each re-counting the list - most keepers open more filters than they apply. 4.9 in place of filtering on mobile; 4.10 to find one tutor by name. 4.11 after every cut, and it decides whether to start reading yet.

questions.question: Which filters should be on to narrow the list?
questions.why: With over 35,000 teachers matching the initial search, applying specific filters for price, availability, and specialties is necessary to find a manageable list of suitable candidates.

questions.why: The screen requires you to select a teaching tool from the dropdown and verify your contact ID so the tutor can successfully connect with you.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to ensure the lesson is conducted on a platform you are comfortable using and that your personal contact ID is accurate.
questions.check: Which tool is selected in the dropdown, and what does the contact ID field contain?
questions.say_example: The lesson runs over <Skype>, and the form needs your Skype name. I don't have it. What is it?

questions.question: Does the lesson tool need a particular browser or app installed first?
questions.why: While selecting Skype or Zoom implies an external app, some platforms' native 'classrooms' only function on specific browsers (like Chrome) or prohibit mobile devices.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user scrambles at the last minute and misses a portion of their paid lesson because they didn't realize they needed to download software or switch devices to support the chosen tool.
questions.check: What does the page say about the classroom's browser or app requirements?
questions.say_example: Noted lessons run in the site's own classroom, which needs <Chrome> and no phones.

questions.question: What should you tell the tutor about your goals and schedule?
questions.why: The form asks for your availability and a message about your goals so the tutor can prepare for the lesson.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might send a generic message or skip schedule preferences, failing to accurately convey your specific learning objectives to the tutor.
questions.check: Does the booking form show a message box, and what is in it?
questions.say_example: Told <tutor> you're preparing for <DELF B1 in March> and can do <weekday evenings>.

questions.question: Do you have any specific files or assignments you want to share with the tutor ahead of the session?
questions.why: The booking form provides an optional feature to upload files, which is useful for giving the tutor materials to review before the lesson.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to proactively send their homework or study materials, which could make the tutoring session more efficient.
questions.check: Does the form show a file upload, and is anything attached?
questions.say_example: Left the file upload empty.

children.label: Confirm the booking
children.note: 7.1 on every commit surface. then one of three: 7.2 to 7.5 on the credit platforms - balance against cost, the wall if it is short, a password as the contract, then Continue; 7.2, 7.6, 7.7 and 7.8 on the card platforms; 7.9 on Wyzant, where the send is the commit. 1.7 can interrupt any of them. seven keepers stop on this goal with the button unpressed (jMRd, eMJV, B6np, zym-, CWIs, cDu8, bD08).

questions.question: What does checkout say happens if the trial isn't a fit?
questions.why: The checkout screen highlights a 'Free replacement or refund' guarantee, reassuring you of your options before finalizing the payment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you miss learning about the platform's satisfaction guarantee and your specific options for a replacement or refund if the tutor isn't a good fit.
questions.check: What guarantee or refund text does the checkout or confirmation show, and did the tutor's profile promise one?
questions.say_example: Noted checkout's promise of a free replacement or refund if the trial isn't a fit.

questions.question: Does the checkout total include the promotion the site promised, like a free trial or first hour?
questions.why: The checkout screen displays the total amount the student is charged for the session, which clarifies the actual cost of the trial.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses accurate information about the financial commitment required for the trial lesson if the agent does not verify the checkout total.
questions.check: What promotion did an earlier page state, and does the checkout total or a discount line show it?
questions.say_example: The profile said the first hour is free. Checkout is charging <60> for it. Something's off, so I've stopped.

questions.question: Was the rewards popup skipped?
questions.why: A 'Rewards found!' popup appeared offering 680 to 1,700 points back, but it was dismissed without being redeemed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user misses out on potential cashback or discount rewards that could have reduced the overall cost of the lesson.
questions.check: Does a rewards popup appear, and what does it offer?
questions.say_example: Skipped the rewards popup offering <680> points. It signs you up for a loyalty program.

questions.question: Does the price in the checkout summary match the rate you selected earlier?
questions.why: This matters because the checkout summary displays a $60 charge for a 1-hour session, contradicting the $20 rate shown previously in the booking panel.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If an agent ignores this discrepancy, you could end up paying significantly more for the session than the advertised rate.
questions.check: What total does the checkout show, and what price and fees were shown on the search card, profile and booking panel?
questions.say_example: Checkout says <60>. The booking panel said <20>. I've stopped until that's explained.

questions.question: Is the checkout total in the same currency as the prices we searched in?
questions.why: Platforms sometimes display search results in a default currency (like USD) but switch to local currency at checkout based on IP or payment method, changing the actual numeric total.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to catch unexpected currency conversion rates or fees that alter the final out-of-pocket cost.
questions.check: What currency code or symbol is on the search-result rates and on the checkout total, and what is the person's currency?
questions.say_example: Prices were in <USD> while we searched. Checkout is in <CAD>. So the total is really <27.50 CAD>.

questions.question: Is your account balance taken off the checkout total?
questions.why: The checkout screen must accurately reflect the application of the $11.00 USD italki Balance shown earlier on the dashboard.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the financial benefit of their existing balance if the agent fails to ensure it is applied during checkout.
questions.check: What balance did the dashboard show, and what does the checkout subtract as balance?
questions.say_example: You had <11> in balance. Checkout isn't using it, so it wants the full <14>. Applying it first.

questions.question: There aren't enough credits for this lesson. Buy more with real money, or stop here?
questions.why: The screen displays an insufficient credits warning with options to either buy more credits or close the modal, forcing a choice on whether to spend real money.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to prevent unwanted financial charges if the agent automatically chooses to buy credits to complete the task.
questions.check: Does the page show an insufficient-credits or balance-short message, a disabled pay button, and the amount still owed?
questions.say_example: You're <30> credits short for this lesson. Buying more means real money, about <3>. Buy them, or stop here?

questions.question: What does typing the password count as agreeing to?
questions.why: Entering the password acts as a legal signature confirming a purchase order and asserting the user is at least 13 years old.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might blindly agree to legal age requirements and contract terms on the user's behalf without their explicit consent.
questions.check: What does the text beside the password field say the entry confirms?
questions.say_example: Noted that typing the password counts as agreeing to the purchase terms and being over <13>.

questions.question: Ready to pay and book this lesson?
questions.why: The payment page shows a final out-of-pocket cost of $3.00 USD, requiring a final decision to either complete the transaction or abandon the booking.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the final opportunity to review the actual cost and back out of the transaction before your funds are spent.
questions.check: What tutor, date, time, length, lesson type, total, payment source, cancellation terms, note to the tutor and commit-button label does the final page show?
questions.say_example: Ready to book. <Ana>, <Tuesday> at <7 pm>, <60> minutes. <14> total, <11> from your balance and <3> on your card. Free to cancel until <Monday 7 pm>. Your note says you're preparing for <DELF B1>. Press to book, or say change.

questions.question: Is there a pre-ticked box that would start a monthly charge after this?
questions.why: Platforms like Preply and Cambly often use discounted trial lessons as entry points into mandatory subscription models, meaning a $5 trial could result in an automatic $100/month charge if not immediately cancelled.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to prevent unwanted recurring charges on their credit card if the agent blindly accepts the trial terms without opting out of the subscription.
questions.check: Does the page show a pre-checked subscription, auto-refill or auto-renew line, and what does it say is charged and when?
questions.say_example: There's a box already ticked that would charge <100> a month after this trial. I've unticked it. Say keep if you want it.

questions.question: After pressing pay, is the page still the checkout with no confirmation or error?
questions.why: Payment gateways sometimes fail silently, dropping the loading animation and leaving the user on the checkout page without generating an explicit error message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might assume the transaction succeeded or get stuck in a loop, leaving the user without a booked lesson.
questions.check: After the pay press, is the page still the checkout with no confirmation, success message or error?
questions.say_example: I pressed pay and nothing changed. No confirmation, no error. I won't press again. Checking your bookings page to see if it went through.

questions.question: Should you resubmit the form now that your email is verified?
questions.why: The 'Tell Us More' form is still displayed with your previously entered message, requiring you to click 'Send' again to actually complete the submission after the email verification step.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that their introductory message to the tutor was successfully transmitted after the email verification interruption.
questions.check: Is the request form still showing with the message filled in and a Send button?
questions.say_example: Your request didn't go out before the email check. It's still here, filled in. Press to send it again.

children.label: Read the outcome
children.note: 8.1 on every commit that lands. 8.2 on the platforms where the tutor still has to accept or reply - italki and Wyzant - and 8.3 where a confirmation email or a dashboard exists. 8.4 to 8.7 as far as the keeper goes: only 7RrY and 7jo_ see past the booking itself, and nobody cancels.

questions.question: Is the lesson booked, or waiting on the tutor to accept?
questions.why: The confirmation screen states that the tutor has 48 hours to accept the request before the lesson is officially scheduled and your credits are deducted.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate understanding that your booking is not yet guaranteed and that you must monitor your account for the tutor's response over the next 48 hours.
questions.check: Does the confirmation say scheduled, or pending the tutor's acceptance, and by when?
questions.say_example: Booked. <Ana>, <Tuesday> at <7 pm>. It's pending until <Ana> accepts, within <48> hours. Credits come off when they do.

questions.question: Does the confirmation page show the date, time and place you booked?
questions.why: Checking the email details like the tutor's name, start date, and location ensures the appointment was booked exactly as you intended.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the personal reassurance of seeing the confirmation email in your inbox to verify the exact meeting location and time.
questions.check: What tutor, date, time and location does the confirmation or lesson details page show, versus what was booked?
questions.say_example: The lesson details page says <Wednesday>. We booked <Tuesday>. I'd check with the tutor before trusting either.

questions.question: Does the expected response time on the confirmation screen match what was stated on the tutor's profile?
questions.why: Verifying that the post-submission screen confirms the two-hour response time promised on the profile ensures your scheduling expectations are accurate.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might overlook the expected response time, leaving you uncertain about when the tutor will actually confirm the lesson.
questions.check: What response time does the confirmation state, and what did the profile state?
questions.say_example: Noted <2> hours to reply on the confirmation, same as the profile.

questions.question: Did the remaining-session count drop by exactly one after booking?
questions.why: The checkout page stated there were 8 sessions left, but the confirmation page showed only 7 remaining, revealing a discrepancy in the account balance.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might overlook this mismatch, leaving you unaware that your subscription balance is incorrect or that an extra session was unexpectedly deducted.
questions.check: What session count did checkout show, and what does the confirmation show?
questions.say_example: Checkout said <8> sessions left. Now it says <6>. That's two gone for one lesson.

questions.question: How did the tutor respond to your message?
questions.why: The screen shows an unread message preview from Kyle M. saying 'Sup dawg', which you need to open to read the full context of their reply.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally evaluate the tutor's communication style and professionalism before committing to a booking.
questions.check: Does the messages panel show a reply from the tutor, with what text and timestamp?
questions.say_example: <Tutor> wrote back within a minute, which is probably an automatic reply. It says <text>.

questions.question: Should I send the tutor another message about this request?
questions.why: The screen displayed a 'Messages' panel with a text box for sending a note to the teacher prior to the lesson.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to provide specific context, goals, or requests to the tutor before the lesson begins.
questions.check: Does the page show a message box to the teacher?
questions.say_example: Skipped a second message to the tutor.

questions.question: Does the countdown on the lesson page match the reply window the confirmation gave?
questions.why: The confirmation screen stated the teacher has 48 hours to respond, which should be immediately reflected as an active countdown on the lesson details page.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the reassurance of personally verifying that the platform's system correctly registered the tutor's response deadline.
questions.check: What countdown does the lesson details page show, and what reply window did the confirmation state?
questions.say_example: Saw a <47> hour countdown for the tutor to reply, matching the <48> hours promised.

questions.question: Does the booking now appear under upcoming sessions on the dashboard?
questions.why: The dashboard displayed an 'Upcoming Sessions' section with the newly booked appointment, confirming the system successfully registered the lesson.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the reassurance of independently verifying that the scheduled lesson is correctly listed in their personal dashboard.
questions.check: Does the dashboard list the new lesson under upcoming sessions?
questions.say_example: Found the lesson under upcoming sessions on the dashboard.

questions.question: Do you consent to having this session recorded and published on YouTube?
questions.why: The confirmation page includes settings for recording consent and YouTube publishing, which directly affect your privacy during the lesson.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might accept the default privacy settings or opt into publishing the recording, potentially exposing your image and voice online without your explicit permission.
questions.check: Does the page show a recording consent or YouTube publishing option, and what is its current state?
questions.say_example: The site wants permission to record your lessons and post them on YouTube. That's yours to decide. Yes or no?
